accessibility: The card is a dialog named "Add a comment"; the message box is labelled the same, the scope select is named "Variant scope", and an error is announced as an alert.
Phones never open this composer; the canvas pill says why there.
constraints: Built only from Adapter Widgets (Stack, Text, Button, Icon, Avatar, TextInput, Select, SelectOption, Alert); no Widget outside the Adapter catalog.

The chips and the states are shown by Variants; the scope is a Select with a field look, not the borderless menu of the app, and its open state shows a listbox. The Comment button's key caps are one hint, not two. The card sits on a plain canvas, not at a click point over a View.
The strings of the app are copied under the same Locale keys; the member name binds through value, the Widget id is an identity, and a diagnostic line is sample content.
Every visible string is bound with $i18n except identities (the Widget type and id, the member name); en-US and zh-TW keep identical key sets.
Visual language follows the Quiet Canvas design system in DESIGN.md.
entryConditions: A reviewer holding the key to write Review threads is in comment mode on a desktop or tablet layout and clicked a Widget, or pressed Comment on View; the composer opens there, 320px wide, with focus in the message box.
The base state is a comment on a Button of the Checkout View with no text yet, scoped to all Variants, and the Comment button disabled until there is text.

The render context selects one Workspace viewport preset, one Locale and one theme; the composer is Workbench chrome, so its text follows the Workbench language and is baked here per Locale. The member name, Widget id and message are sample content.
spec.intent: Show the inline composer of the Workbench canvas as built from Adapter Widgets only: the small card that opens at the click point when a reviewer comments on a Widget, or on the View as a whole. What the comment is about, whether it applies to this Variant or all of them, the message, who is commenting, and what happens when it cannot be sent.
interactionRules: The header always states the anchor of the new thread: the Widget type and id, or Whole View (an icon and the words) for a comment on the View as a whole, which is anchored to the RootShell; nothing is ever created without one.

While the Preview shows a Variant, the scope choice offers This Variant or All Variants (the default); a thread scoped to this Variant is limited to it, All Variants means every current and future Variant. With no Variant shown, the scope is the words All Variants and not a choice.
Comment, or ⌘↵ (Ctrl Enter), posts the thread and its first message; Cancel closes it. Cancel or Esc with text asks Discard this comment? first, Keep editing or Discard.
A failed post keeps the text and says so; Retry sends again. When the thread was created and its message was not, the alert says so and Retry posts only the message.
